rules.title: Function signature monomorphization substitutes type params
rules.statement: Monomorphizing a function clones its signature applying the type substitution s to the return type and to every non-variadic parameter type; non-type signature attributes (name, package, extern/vararg flags, local slot count, lifetime params, lifetime outlives) are preserved verbatim.

rules.title: Variadic type-pack parameter expands to N concrete params
rules.statement: A variadic parameter whose type is a TypeVar pack P, when P is bound in the pack map to a list of N types, expands into N distinct parameters named `<param>$<i>` (i in 0..N), each typed by the i-th pack member; if P is not bound the parameter is dropped.
rules.uncertainty: Expanded name form `make_pack_arg_name` inferred from call; exact separator defined elsewhere.

rules.title: Closure types automatically satisfy Fn/FnMut/FnOnce
rules.statement: Every closure type (canonical name beginning with `|`, i.e. `|T1,...| -> R`) is treated as implementing Fn, FnMut, and FnOnce without any explicit `impl`; the trait engine answers satisfies(Fn-family, closure) = true.

rules.title: Blanket impl bounds combine conjunctively; empty bounds = impl-for-all
rules.statement: A blanket impl is satisfied iff ALL of its bounds hold (primary bound first, then extra bounds, conjoined). A blanket impl with empty primary bound and no extras is an unconditional impl-for-all (always satisfied).

rules.title: Reference-type impl lookup key is structure-aware
rules.statement: An `impl Trait for &T` / `&mut T` is keyed by structure: prefix `$ref_`/`$mut_ref_` followed by the struct name when the pointee is a (possibly zoned) struct, otherwise followed by the full ref's type string; `&&i32` and `&i32` thus resolve to distinct keys (no `&`-stripping collision).

rules.title: str impls are keyed under &[u8]'s wire form
rules.statement: For impl lookup, the concrete type `&[u8]` is the canonical wire form of `str`; a concrete name of `&[u8]` is renamed to `str` before bound checking so impls registered for `str` apply.
rules.uncertainty: Mirrors a legacy enum bound check; direction (str↔&[u8]) is normative for lookup keys only.

rules.title: Generic instantiation bound satisfaction recurses into type-args
rules.statement: For a generic struct/enum instantiation, satisfying `Concrete<A..>: Trait` requires not only that a matching impl exists by bare name, but also that for each impl type-param, after unifying the impl target pattern against Concrete, every bound on that param holds for the unified argument (recursively). Non-generic / argument-free concrete types are accepted on the bare-name impl check alone.

rules.title: Fn-family bound satisfied by callable shapes intrinsically
rules.statement: A parenthesized Fn/FnMut/FnOnce bound is satisfied intrinsically (no registered impl needed) by any fn-value kind, Closure, TypeVar (deferred to outer mono pass), or Struct/ZonedStruct (struct-with-Fn-impl bridge); any other kind fails the bound.

rules.title: Method where-bounds gate method instantiation
rules.statement: A method with a where-bound `Subject: Trait` is only instantiated for a concrete substitution if the substituted Subject satisfies Trait; if the substituted Subject still contains a TypeVar the check is deferred to an outer mono pass (not a failure). Unsatisfied where-bounds suppress synthesis of that method.

rules.title: Auto-trait bounds checked structurally, not via impls
rules.statement: When a method type-param bound names an auto trait, satisfaction is decided by structural auto-trait analysis of the concrete type (is_auto_satisfied) rather than by impl lookup.

rules.title: HRTB bound satisfaction requires universal-position, bijective lifetime mapping
rules.statement: When a trait bound carries lifetime type-args, the bound's lifetimes must align with the impl's lifetime params: a bound lifetime that is empty/'static must match exactly or map to a universally-quantified impl lifetime; a named bound lifetime requires the impl side be universal and the impl-lt→bound-lt map be 1-1 (injective). An impl outlives constraint `'a: 'b` where both sides map to bound-side binder (skolem) lifetimes is unsatisfiable and rejected.
rules.uncertainty: Region soundness rule; full statement deferred to sema_collect region_ok per comment.

rules.title: Struct repr/zone markers preserved through monomorphization
rules.statement: Cloning a generic struct to a monomorphic instance preserves its markers: zoned, self-describing, rel-ptr, borrow-carrying, zone-mut, zoned2, non-null, union, and lifetime params/outlives; type_params are cleared (result is monomorphic).

rules.title: DST-ness inherited when last field instantiates to unsized
rules.statement: A monomorphized struct becomes a custom-DST if, after substitution, its LAST field has an unsized type (UnsizedSlice or UnsizedDyn); the template's own DST flag is otherwise preserved.

rules.title: Struct methods renamed from Base__m to Instance__m on clone
rules.statement: When a generic struct is monomorphized to a new name, each method `Base__method` is renamed to `<new_name>__method`, preserving any package prefix before the bare name.

rules.title: Concrete impl method overrides blanket method for that instantiation
rules.statement: If a non-generic function exists whose bare name equals the renamed method name (a user-written concrete `impl Foo<Concrete>` method), the blanket `impl<T> Foo<T>` method is NOT cloned for that instantiation; the concrete definition is used instead.

rules.title: Structured-impl method skipped when its self pattern mismatches
rules.statement:
For a method from a structured-self impl (e.g. `impl Pin<&T>` on `struct Pin

`), impl-level params are bound by unifying the impl target pattern's args against the concrete struct args; if unification of any decidable arg fails, the method does not belong to this instantiation and is not cloned. Args still containing TypeVars, or projection/associated-type args, are skipped (deferred / not structurally decidable) rather than failing.

rules.title: Methods present in prebuilt archive get signature-only stubs
rules.statement: If a method's final (renamed) name is present in the binary-symbol set (body in a prebuilt stdlib archive), only its signature is cloned (no body); code-gen skips body emission and relies on the archive.

rules.title: Generic struct methods cloned lazily on demand
rules.statement: In lazy-methods mode, a generic struct (non-empty type_params) is cloned with an empty METHODS array; its methods are cloned on demand later (call-site / dispatch pin / root pin), with the bound gate applied at that time.
